title: The Decision to Deploy
summary: Work through The Decision to Deploy.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **The Decision to Deploy**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Deployment Release, § The Decision to Deploy
blocks.md: Verification left the machine with a signed set of fault records. Each pairs an observed trace under an injected fault (a stalled proposer, a stale frame, lost fieldbus frames, a sagging bus) with an oracle fixed before the trial, and the set names the operating regimes no trial reached. Beside it sit the records the earlier chapters produced: the authority record of arbitration and fallback outcomes, the placement record of compute scheduling and isolation, and the evaluation record of closed-loop task performance.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Release manifest matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: The release manifest binds every upstream record, the argument digest, binary hashes, calibration, standing conditions, wear budget, expiry, and the adjudicator's signature to one configuration and gates motion fail-closed.

questions.q: The section **The Decision to Deploy** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Release adjudicates physical inequalities (stop inside the clear distance, contact force under the assessed limit, WCET inside its deadline) through a claim-argument-evidence case whose warrants say why each piece of evidence supports its claim.
Fleet exposure narrows intervals for common outcomes but leaves rare severe outcomes wide, so each outcome's claim is licensed separately and disclosed.

The release manifest binds every upstream record, the argument digest, binary hashes, calibration, standing conditions, wear budget, expiry, and the adjudicator's signature to one configuration and gates motion fail-closed.
A contained canary qualifies an update by a non-inferiority test on the intervention-rate ratio against a margin declared in advance, with sequential stopping.
